Plompy Engine and LocalSource guide · 2026-11-18

Documentation/Discord engine

Run Plompy from Discord

The original engine accepts tasks from private Discord threads, stores work in a durable queue and launches a coding runner. That deployment uses the engine repository's compose.yaml, its private environment file, its runner credentials and its own volumes.

Start the stable Discord engine#

1. Prepare a Discord bot and a private forum in a server you own. Enable Message Content Intent and copy your server, owner, bot and forum IDs. See Discord configuration for permissions. 2. Use Git to clone release v0.13.0 for its Compose file and follow the Docker engine first start. The Docker image uses Codex. For a Linux service using an experimental Claude Code or OpenCode runner, follow host deployment. 3. After the structured ready event, run the first private code goal.

If you already run the engine, use your existing private environment and volumes. For an upgrade from before 0.12, follow the migration guide.

Personal assistant preview#

The personal assistant preview adds notes, tasks and one-time reminders in a dedicated thread in the configured private forum. It requires the 1.0.0-alpha.1 engine image and explicit opt-in.

For MCP tools in a host agent, use the Local Docker quickstart. Its local or local-browser service runs in a separate Compose project with separate private volumes.

Existing documentation#

  • Runner support and boundaries
  • Runner integrations
  • State backups

Different OpenCode roles#

In Discord mode, the engine's experimental OpenCode adapter starts the pinned runner to execute a job. In local mode, your independently running OpenCode client calls Plompy's tools.

Do not point the host client at an engine-managed private runner directory. Do not copy Discord memory, bot credentials or runner auth into the local artifact volume.
